title: Armenia and Azerbaijan clash along the Tavush–Tovuz border section
body:
Armed clashes between Armenian and Azerbaijani forces began on 12 July 2020 along the state border between Armenia's Tavush Province and Azerbaijan's Tovuz District, away from the Nagorno-Karabakh line of contact. The first fighting took place near Movses on the Armenian side and near Agdam village on the Azerbaijani side. Each government blamed the other for starting the fighting. The International Crisis Group said violence erupted after an Azerbaijani military vehicle drove close to the border near Movses, while Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov pointed to Armenia's restored checkpoint. The fighting was conducted mainly with artillery and drones rather than infantry assaults.

Casualty figures conflicted. Armenia reported six soldiers killed and about 35 servicemen wounded. Azerbaijan reported twelve servicemen killed, along with one civilian, 76-year-old Aziz Azizov, in Agdam, and four soldiers wounded. The Azerbaijani dead included Major General Polad Hashimov, chief of staff of the 3rd Corps, and Colonel Ilgar Mirzayev. None of these claims was independently verified. Armenia's Foreign Ministry accused Azerbaijan of targeting civilians and Armenia appealed to its CSTO allies, while President Ilham Aliyev blamed Armenia's military-political leadership and raised the civilian death with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on 22 July.

The clashes occurred close to the so-called Ganja gap, an energy and transport corridor important to Azerbaijan. Dozens of ceasefire violations per day were reported by both sides through late July. Both sides claimed victory and the front returned to the status quo before hostilities. Fighting resumed on 27 September 2020 in Nagorno-Karabakh itself and grew into the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War.
